artiest/shelly-manne.text:
Shelly Manne was an American jazz drummer, born in Manhattan in 1920. His father and uncles were drummers. He grew up taking the swing drummers Jo Jones and Dave Tough as his models and developed his style in the clubs of 52nd Street. In 1940 he landed his first job with a well-known big band, the orchestra of Bobby Byrne. He recorded with Coleman Hawkins and played with Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker as bebop emerged. In the late 1940s and early 1950s he became a star with Woody Herman and Stan Kenton.

In the early 1950s he settled in Los Angeles, on a ranch where he and his wife kept horses. There he became a leading figure of West Coast Jazz. He played with Shorty Rogers, Art Pepper, Chet Baker and Hampton Hawes, among others, and recorded extensively for Contemporary Records. In 1959 his quintet recorded live for three days at the Black Hawk in San Francisco, which yielded four LPs. His 1953 album The West Coast Sound, with specially commissioned compositions, shows the tightly arranged, cool style. He himself did not like being pigeonholed.

Manne was versatile. He played Dixieland, swing, bebop, avant-garde jazz and later fusion, and performed on hundreds of Hollywood films and television programmes. Albums such as West Side Story from 1960 and Daktari from 1967 show his range. He died in 1984. Manne showed that a drummer can be a soloist and a colourful accompanist at the same time.
artiest/shelly-manne.listen: Listen to Shelly Manne's West Side Story and notice the drumming: how he supports Bernstein's melodies with colour and short accents instead of merely keeping time.

artiest/shigeru-umebayashi.text: Shigeru Umebayashi (born 1951) first played in a Japanese rock band and then turned to writing film music. He became internationally known through Wong Kar-wai's In the Mood for Love (2000). Its best-known piece, Yumeji's Theme, was originally written for the Japanese film Yumeji (1991) by Seijun Suzuki. It is a slow waltz for strings with pizzicato accompaniment, which Wong Kar-wai repeats again and again over slow-motion images. For 2046 (2004) Umebayashi wrote a large part of the music. With Zhang Yimou he made Shi mian mai fu (2004). His style is melodic, melancholic and close to European Romanticism.
artiest/shigeru-umebayashi.listen: Listen to the three-beat rhythm of the waltz and to the way the cello plays the melody, singing and with plenty of rubato.

artiest/shirley-bassey.text:
Shirley Bassey is a Welsh singer, born in 1937 in Tiger Bay in Cardiff, the youngest of six children. Her father came from Nigeria, her mother from England. At school she received little encouragement for her powerful voice. At fourteen she went to work in a steel factory and sang in pubs and clubs in the evenings and at weekends. In 1953 she signed her first professional contract, for a tour with the revue Memories of Jolson. In 1955 she was discovered by the impresario Jack Hylton and given a part in a West End show. Record producer Johnny Franz then offered her a contract with Philips.

In 1959 she became the first Welsh singer with a number 1 in the United Kingdom. In the decades that followed she had many hits, including As I Love You and History Repeating. She is the only artist to have sung more than one official theme song for a James Bond film: Goldfinger in 1964, Diamonds Are Forever in 1971 and Moonraker in 1979. Goldfinger entered the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2008. In 1977 she received the first Brit Award for best British female solo artist, and in 1999 she was made a Dame.

Her voice is powerful and dramatic, with a wide range that suits large orchestras and grand gestures. On albums such as Shirley Stops the Shows and I Am What I Am she sang both ballads and showpieces. She was a favourite singer of Aretha Franklin and influenced other vocalists. Together with the strings and brass of the orchestral arrangements, her Bond songs form a sound that belongs to the spy films.
artiest/shirley-bassey.listen: Listen to Goldfinger and notice the way she holds the long final note above the menacing brass and strings.

artiest/shirley-collins.text:
Shirley Collins is an English folk singer, born in 1935 in Hastings, East Sussex. She grew up in a family that loved traditional songs and learned a great deal from her grandfather and an aunt. At seventeen she went to a teacher training college in London, where she became involved in the early folk revival. In 1954 she met the American song collector Alan Lomax. In 1959 she travelled with him through the southern United States, where they recorded many songs. Part of those recordings was released as Sounds of the South.

In 1958 she recorded her first albums, Sweet England and False True Lovers, on which she accompanied herself on banjo. In 1964 she made Folk Roots, New Routes with the guitarist Davey Graham, a blend of jazz and folk. After that she worked mainly with her sister Dolly, who played piano and portative organ, on albums including The Sweet Primeroses and The Power of the True Love Knot. On Anthems in Eden from 1969, David Munrow and his Early Music Consort played period instruments such as rebecs, sackbuts, fiddle and crumhorn. In 1971 she married Ashley Hutchings, with whom she formed the Albion Country Band and the Etchingham Steam Band. After a painful divorce she lost her voice to dysphonia and gave up music. In 2016 she returned with Lodestar.

Her singing has a clear, sober, almost unadorned sound, without grand gestures. She showed how old songs could sound new with modern ideas, and she became a model for later folk musicians.
artiest/shirley-collins.listen: Listen to Barbara Allen and notice her voice: it is simple and without ornament. Hear how the story of the song and the plain accompaniment carry each other.

artiest/shirley-walker.text: Shirley Walker (1945–2006) was a pianist who for years worked as an orchestrator and conductor for other composers, among them Danny Elfman on Batman (1989). For Batman: The Animated Series (1992) she became head composer and musical director. She led a team of composers and had every episode recorded with a real orchestra, which was rare for animated series. Every villain was given a theme of his own. For the feature film Batman: Mask of the Phantasm (1993) she wrote a gothic score with choir. She was one of the first women to score a major Hollywood film as sole composer. Later she also wrote horror music, for example for Final Destination (2000).
artiest/shirley-walker.listen: Listen for the choir and the heavy brass in a dark minor key, and for the short themes that belong to a single character.

artiest/shivkumar-sharma.text:
Shivkumar Sharma was an Indian classical musician and santoor player. He is regarded as the man who made the santoor suitable for Indian classical music. The santoor is a hammered dulcimer that was originally a folk instrument from Kashmir. Sharma was born in Jammu in 1938. His father, a singer and tabla player, taught him to sing and play tabla at the age of five and later introduced him to the santoor. He began on the instrument at thirteen and gave his first public concert in Mumbai in 1955, playing Raga Yaman for an hour.

He recorded his first solo album in 1960. In 1967 he made the concept album Call of the Valley with the flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia and the guitarist Brij Bhushan Kabra, which became one of the great successes of Indian classical music. In 1968 he gave his first concert abroad, in Los Angeles. With Chaurasia he formed the duo Shiv-Hari, which wrote music for Hindi films such as Silsila, Faasle, Chandni, Lamhe and Darr. He also played tabla on a song from the film Guide. He himself described classical music not as entertainment but as a meditative journey.

His instrument has a hundred strings, struck with small wooden mallets, and produces long, floating lines and fast runs. Sharma received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1986 and later the Padma Shri and the Padma Bhushan. From 1996 he played together with his son Rahul. He died in 2022. Thanks to him, the santoor is known worldwide.
artiest/shivkumar-sharma.listen: Listen to Call of the Valley and notice the santoor: the bright, almost glittering tone of the mallets against the softer flute, which together seem to paint a landscape.

artiest/shivkumar-sharma-brij-bhushan-ka.text:
In 1967 the santoor player Shivkumar Sharma, the slide guitarist Brij Bhushan Kabra and the bansuri player Hariprasad Chaurasia recorded the instrumental album Call of the Valley together. It became a milestone of world music and one of the best-known records of Indian classical music. The critic Ken Hunt wrote that a newcomer who buys only one Indian classical record should make it this one. The album is also included in the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die. It also marked the beginning of the long collaboration between Chaurasia and Sharma.

Hariprasad Chaurasia, born in Allahabad in 1938, grew up with his father, a wrestler. He learned music in secret and later became a pupil of Annapurna Devi of the Maihar gharana, who made it a condition that he unlearn everything. He has played left-handed ever since. In 1957 he started at All India Radio in Cuttack, and in 1962 he moved to Bombay. Together with Sharma he formed, as Shiv-Hari, a film composer duo, for Silsila and Chandni among others. He also worked with George Harrison, Zakir Hussain, John McLaughlin and Jan Garbarek, and played on The Inner Light by The Beatles.

Chaurasia raised the bansuri, a bamboo transverse flute, to the status of a concert instrument, with a singing tone and an extended development of the raga, with alap, jor and jhala. Sharma's santoor and Kabra's slide guitar give the album its voice. In this way the trio brought Indian classical music to a worldwide audience.
artiest/shivkumar-sharma-brij-bhushan-ka.listen: Listen to Ahir Bhairav / Nat Bhairav and notice how the bansuri, the santoor and the slide guitar hand the melody to one another. Follow how the music starts slowly and only later speeds up.

artiest/shocking-blue.text:
Shocking Blue was a beat group from The Hague, founded in 1967 by the guitarist and songwriter Robbie van Leeuwen. He had previously played in The Motions. In 1968 the singer Mariska Veres joined, and with her low, powerful voice she became the face of the band. Shocking Blue belongs to Nederbeat: Dutch guitar bands that sang in English. The group is important because it was the first Dutch band to top the American chart.

Van Leeuwen wrote Venus, a short song built on a simple guitar riff, with a chorus you can sing along to after hearing it once. Veres sings it without embellishment, and the record even contains a typing error: 'godness' instead of 'goddess'. In the Netherlands the single reached number 3 in the Veronica Top 40 in July 1969. It was released in America and Britain at the end of 1969, and in February 1970 Venus spent one week at the top of the Billboard Hot 100. Other hits were Mighty Joe (1969) and Never Marry a Railroad Man (1970). The band broke up in 1974.

Van Leeuwen's songs outlived the group. The British girl group Bananarama made Venus an American number 1 again in 1986, this time in the hi-NRG sound of the production trio Stock Aitken Waterman. Nirvana recorded Love Buzz, from the Shocking Blue album At Home (1969), in 1988 as their first single and later put it on Bleach (1989). In this way a line runs from a beat band from The Hague to the grunge of Seattle. Mariska Veres died in The Hague in 2006.
artiest/shocking-blue.listen: Venus (1969): notice the guitar riff in the intro. It strongly resembles the opening of Pinball Wizard by The Who, and it returns throughout the song beneath Mariska Veres's voice.

artiest/shorty-rogers.text:
Shorty Rogers, born Milton Rajonsky, was an American jazz musician and one of the most important creators of West Coast Jazz. He played trumpet and flugelhorn and was in great demand as an arranger. He was born in 1924 in Great Barrington, Massachusetts, and first worked with Will Bradley and Red Norvo. From 1947 to 1949 he played extensively with Woody Herman, and in 1950 and 1951 with Stan Kenton. He then joined the Lighthouse All Stars in Los Angeles and led groups of his own.

From 1953 to 1962 he recorded a series of albums for RCA Victor, such as Courts the Count in 1954, and with his group Shorty Rogers and His Giants for Atlantic, such as The Swinging Mr. Rogers in 1955 and Martians Come Back. Those records partly contain avant-garde music. They can partly be described as Cool Jazz, but they also look back to the hot style of Count Basie, whom Rogers always named as a major inspiration. On Jazz Composers Workshop from 1955 he played with Shelly Manne, among others.

In 1957 Rogers wrote the music for the Warner Bros. cartoon Three Little Bops and later for films such as Tarzan, the Ape Man. He did more and more work in the Hollywood studios. He died in 1994. Rogers shows how the tight arrangements and light sound of West Coast Jazz could also be playful, sometimes with a wink.
artiest/shorty-rogers.listen: Listen to Martians Go Home from The Swinging Mr. Rogers and notice the interplay of trumpet, saxophones and drums: tightly arranged, but with plenty of space and humour.

artiest/showtek.text:
Showtek is a Dutch dance duo from Eindhoven, consisting of the brothers Wouter and Sjoerd Janssen. They started in 2001 with techno and switched to hardstyle in 2003. Wouter mainly made hard trance under the name Walt, and Sjoerd hardstyle as Duro. Their first album, Today Is Tomorrow, was released in 2007 on their own label Dutch Master Works. In 2009 came Analogue Players in a Digital World, which was presented at the Amsterdam Dance Event.

Later they switched from hardstyle to house music. From 2011 they worked with Tiësto, and in 2012 they started Crazy Collabs, a series of collaborations with producers from other genres, such as Tiësto, Hardwell and Justin Prime. They also contributed to Nobody's Perfect by Chris Brown. In 2013 they founded the label Skink, licensed to Spinnin Records. In 2014 they made Bad with David Guetta and Vassy, and in 2016 Believer with Major Lazer. In 2014 they ranked 17th in the list of best DJs, in 2016 96th.

Their sound revolves around hard, pounding basses, tight rhythms and big, dancefloor-oriented drops. In 2023 they returned to hardstyle after fifteen years, with a performance at Qlimax, and in 2024 the hardstyle album 360 Blue was released. Showtek shows how a Dutch hardstyle scene grew into international dance music.
artiest/showtek.listen: Listen to Bad with David Guetta and notice the build-up: the lyrics and melody build, and then a hard, rhythmic drop follows.

artiest/shuggie-otis.text:
Shuggie Otis is an American singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist, born in Los Angeles in 1953. He is the son of the rhythm and blues musician and bandleader Johnny Otis. He started on guitar at the age of two and at eleven played professionally in his father's band, sometimes wearing dark glasses and a fake moustache to get into nightclubs. Growing up among blues, jazz and R&B musicians, he was captivated above all by the music of his own generation: Jimi Hendrix, Arthur Lee of Love and Sly Stone.

In 1969, at the age of fifteen, he recorded an album in a single weekend with Al Kooper, the Kooper Session. That same year his first solo album, Here Comes Shuggie Otis, was released on Epic Records. B.B. King called him his favourite new guitarist. He also played with Frank Zappa, including on electric bass on Peaches en Regalia, and with Etta James. His best-known album was Freedom Flight in 1971, with Strawberry Letter 23. The Brothers Johnson made that song a hit, after a tip to the producer Quincy Jones.

In 1974 came Inspiration Information, his third and last album for Epic. He wrote and arranged all the songs himself and played nearly all the instruments, except for the horns and some of the strings. He turned down an invitation to tour with the Rolling Stones. After that he dropped out of sight. Much later, listeners rediscovered his work as a remarkable mix of soul, funk, blues and psychedelia. Shuggie Otis shows how a single musician can build an entirely personal sound on his own.
artiest/shuggie-otis.listen: Listen to Inspiration Information and notice how everything in the song is built by a single musician: a soft beat, a warm bass line and the gently flowing guitar.

artiest/sid-catlett.text:
Sid Catlett, nicknamed Big Sid, was an American jazz drummer, born in Evansville, Indiana, in 1910. As a child he had piano and drum lessons, and in Chicago he got his first drum kit. There he absorbed the styles of drummers such as Zutty Singleton and Baby Dodds. In 1928 he played with Darnell Howard and then with the orchestra of Sammy Stewart in New York. In the 1930s he played and recorded with Benny Carter, McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Fletcher Henderson and Don Redman.

From 1938 to 1942 he was the regular drummer in Louis Armstrong's big band, and from 1947 to 1949 he played with Armstrong's All-Stars. He also played occasionally with Benny Goodman and, briefly in 1945, with Duke Ellington. He was one of the few drummers who made the move to bebop without difficulty, and in 1945 he played on recordings by Dizzy Gillespie. He appeared on screen in the film Jammin' the Blues, but the drums on the soundtrack were played by Jo Jones. He died in 1951 of a heart attack, during a benefit concert in Chicago.

Catlett was known as tasteful, steady and supportive. He wanted his sound to merge with that of the whole group and asked soloists what they wanted: brushes, sticks or the Chinese cymbal. Earl Hines said he seemed to know what you were going to play before you knew it yourself. His solos sounded structured, with variations and sudden silences, and he was also a showman who bounced his sticks. His son Sid became an NBA basketball player.
artiest/sid-catlett.listen: Listen to a 1940s recording of Louis Armstrong with Sid Catlett and notice the drums: he keeps the beat tight, but never plays over the soloist.

artiest/sid-vicious.text:
Sid Vicious, born Simon John Ritchie, was an English musician, best known as the second bass player of the punk band the Sex Pistols. He was born in London in 1957, grew up in Tunbridge Wells and later in Hackney. On a photography course he met John Lydon, the future Johnny Rotten. Lydon gave him the nickname Sid Vicious after Ritchie was bitten by Lydon's hamster Sid, named after Syd Barrett. He hung around Malcolm McLaren and Vivienne Westwood's fashion shop Sex and so came into the circle around the Sex Pistols.

In 1976 he belonged to the circle of musicians around Siouxsie and the Banshees, for whom he drummed once, and to the Flowers of Romance, who never performed or recorded. In February 1977 he replaced Glen Matlock in the Sex Pistols, at McLaren's initiative. He could barely play. On the debut album Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols, the guitarist Steve Jones played virtually all the bass. That album was released in 1977 and went straight to number 1 in the United Kingdom. It is often called the most influential punk album. Vicious became the face of the nihilistic side of punk and became addicted to heroin.

In 1977 he met Nancy Spungen. She died in New York in 1978, after which he was charged. He himself died in 1979, aged 21, of an overdose. After his death Sid Sings was released, featuring among other things his vocals on Born to Lose, recorded at a Christmas concert for the children of firefighters in 1977. He remained an icon of punk culture.
artiest/sid-vicious.listen: Listen to Sid Sings and notice Born to Lose: it is a raw live recording in which you can hear that it is a performance and not a polished studio record.

artiest/sidiki-diabate.text:
Sidiki Diabaté is a Malian kora player, singer and music producer, born in Bamako in 1992. He is the son of the kora player Toumani Diabaté and the grandson of his namesake Sidiki Diabaté. He belongs to the 77th generation of a family of griots, musicians who preserve and pass on the history of their people. In his family almost all the musicians are kora players. His uncle Mamadou Sidiki Diabaté plays the kora, and so does Sona Jobarteh, a cousin of his father, who is a well-known kora player and the first female kora player from a griot family.

The kora is a West African harp with a large calabash as its resonating body and a long neck. His best-known record is Toumani & Sidiki from 2014, an album on which father and son play together. In 2016 came Diabateba Music, Vol. 1. Since 2015 he has been a member of the musical collective Lamomali, led by Matthieu Chedid.

With his work he continues a long tradition, but he also connects it with younger forms. Anyone who hears Toumani & Sidiki hears two generations in conversation. In 2020 he was arrested on suspicion of assaulting a former girlfriend.
artiest/sidiki-diabate.listen: Listen to a track from Toumani & Sidiki and notice how the two koras complement each other, without either one drowning out the other.

artiest/sidney-bechet.text: Sidney Bechet of New Orleans was the first great soloist on the soprano saxophone, alongside the clarinet. His playing had a broad, fast vibrato and enormous power. In 1919 he played in Europe with the orchestra of Will Marion Cook; the Swiss conductor Ernest Ansermet then wrote a famous tribute to him. In 1939 he recorded Summertime for the new label Blue Note, one of its first successes. After the war he settled in France, where he became a great star. His own melody Petite fleur became a hit all across Europe in the 1950s. He died near Paris in 1959.
artiest/sidney-bechet.listen: Notice the broad vibrato of the soprano saxophone: every long note trembles.

artiest/simon-en-garfunkel.text:
Simon & Garfunkel was an American duo of the singer-songwriter Paul Simon and the singer Art Garfunkel. They met in 1953 at school in Queens, New York, and learned to harmonise together there, while Simon began writing songs. As teenagers they had a small success under the name Tom & Jerry with Hey Schoolgirl from 1957, an imitation of their heroes, the Everly Brothers. In 1963 they started again, this time with an interest in folk, and signed with Columbia Records. Their debut album Wednesday Morning, 3 A.M. from 1964 sold poorly, after which Simon went to England and Garfunkel continued his studies.

In 1965 a new, remixed version of The Sound of Silence became a radio hit and reached the top of the Billboard Hot 100. The album Sounds of Silence followed in 1966, as did Parsley, Sage, Rosemary and Thyme, on which they had more creative control. Their music was given a prominent place in the 1967 film The Graduate. In 1968 the soundtrack album topped the album chart, as did Bookends with Mrs. Robinson. Their last studio album, Bridge over Troubled Water, was released in January 1970, just before the split, and became one of the best-selling albums in the world. The Boxer, Cecilia and America are also part of their work.

The duo combined folk with rock, two-part harmony and poetic lyrics. After the split Simon had a successful solo career, with Graceland among others, and Garfunkel sang hits such as Bright Eyes. Their 1981 concert in Central Park possibly drew more than 500,000 people. In 1990 they were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/simon-en-garfunkel.listen: Listen to The Sound of Silence and notice how the two voices sing together at the same pitch. Follow how the accompaniment begins with a simple acoustic guitar and later adds more instruments.

artiest/simon-le-bon.text:
Simon Le Bon is an English singer, born in 1958. He is best known as lead singer and lyricist of the new wave band Duran Duran and of the side project Arcadia. At the age of six he did a screen test for a TV commercial, he sang in a church choir and trained as an actor. In 1978 he worked on a kibbutz in the Negev and then studied drama in Birmingham. In 1980 he was introduced to the fledgling band Duran Duran.

The band had been founded in 1978 by childhood friends John Taylor and Nick Rhodes and had a solid rhythm section, with disco, funk and electronics on top. Only the singer was still missing. Le Bon came to audition in May 1980 with a notebook full of poems he had written himself, some of which later ended up on the first albums. Within six weeks the band was playing regularly in Birmingham, London and Nottingham. In December 1980 a contract with EMI followed. The debut album Duran Duran was released in 1981. Rio followed in 1982 and Seven and the Ragged Tiger in 1983. The band became famous as part of the New Romantics. Le Bon also sang on the charity single Do They Know It's Christmas?. In 1993 the band returned with the Wedding Album and the single Ordinary World, which he later sang together with Luciano Pavarotti.

His voice and his lyrics help shape the sound of Duran Duran: a pop sound with a solid rock foundation. He received three Ivor Novello Awards, including one for his contribution to British music, and an MBE in 2024. Duran Duran showed how electronics and danceable pop could conquer the charts together in the early 1980s.
artiest/simon-le-bon.listen: Listen to Ordinary World from the Wedding Album and notice Le Bon's voice: restrained and melodious, unlike the danceable up-tempo hits of the early 1980s.

artiest/simon-phillips.text:
Simon Phillips is an English drummer, songwriter and producer in jazz fusion and rock, born in 1957 and living in the United States. At twelve he began playing professionally in the Dixieland band of his father, Sid Phillips. After his father's death he switched to pop and rock and got work in a production of the musical Jesus Christ Superstar, which led to other session work.

In the 1970s he played with Jeff Beck, Gil Evans, Stanley Clarke, Peter Gabriel, Pete Townshend and Frank Zappa. He was the drummer in 801, the supergroup of Phil Manzanera and Brian Eno, on the album 801 Live from 1976. On Judas Priest's Sin After Sin from 1977 he introduced the double bass drum that later became defining for heavy metal, especially thrash metal. He played with Michael Schenker and Mike Rutherford, and in 1981 he formed the new wave band Ph.D. In 1989 he played on The Who's American reunion tour. That same year he recorded his first solo album, Protocol, on which he played all the instruments. He also played uncredited on Elektrobank by The Chemical Brothers.

In 1992 Toto asked him to replace the late Jeff Porcaro. He remained the band's drummer until 2014. After that he focused on his solo work, including the Protocol series. Phillips shows that a session drummer can put a personal stamp on very different styles.
artiest/simon-phillips.listen: Listen to Dissident Aggressor on Judas Priest's Sin After Sin and notice the fast double bass drum, the example of what later became common in metal.

artiest/simon-rattle.text:
Sir Simon Rattle is a British conductor, born in Liverpool in 1955. He played piano and violin, but first worked as a percussionist in the Merseyside Youth Orchestra. In 1971 he went to the Royal Academy of Music, and in 1974, his graduation year, he won the John Player International Conducting Competition. After a performance of Mahler's Second Symphony at the academy he was discovered by an impresario. At twenty he joined the opera at Glyndebourne, where over 28 years he conducted more than two hundred performances.

His breakthrough came with the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra. He was its principal conductor from 1980 and music director from 1990 until 1998. He set up the series Towards the Millennium, with twentieth-century music, and oversaw the move to the new Symphony Hall in 1991. From 2002 to 2018 he was chief conductor of the Berliner Philharmoniker, from 2017 to 2023 music director of the London Symphony Orchestra, and since 2023 chief conductor of the Bavarian Radio Symphony Orchestra. He was knighted in 1994.

His recordings are wide-ranging: from Mahler and Sibelius to Holst and Messiaen, and from War Requiem to Porgy and Bess and The Jazz Album. He also supports youth music and works with youth orchestras. As principal guest conductor of the Orchestra of the Age of Enlightenment he also led performances on period instruments. Rattle made classical music appealing to a wide audience.
artiest/simon-rattle.listen: Listen to The Planets from 1987 and notice the great contrasts between the fierce, rhythmic sections and the calm, soft ones.

artiest/simone-kermes.text:
Simone Kermes is a German coloratura soprano, born in Leipzig in 1965. She is known for her virtuoso voice, which is especially suited to the opera seria of the Baroque and the early Classical period. She has sung in many major theatres and concert halls, including the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées in Paris, the Brooklyn Academy of Music in New York and the Staatsoper in Stuttgart. She was also a guest at festivals such as the Schwetzinger Festspiele, the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival and the Bachfest in Leipzig.

On the opera stage she has sung countless Handel heroines, such as Adelaide in Lotario, Asteria in Tamerlano and the title roles in Alcina and Rodelinda. She also sang Mozart, as Konstanze in Die Entführung aus dem Serail, Fiordiligi in Così fan tutte and Donna Anna in Don Giovanni. In 2000 she sang in Schwetzingen in the first modern performance of La divisione del mondo by Legrenzi, and in 2014 the role of La Folie in Platée by Rameau in Vienna and New York.

Her records show the same breadth. She recorded Handel operas, such as Rodelinda and Lotario, but also Vivaldi in Amor sacro and Amor profano, Arias for Cuzzoni in La Diva and Bel Canto: From Monteverdi to Verdi. In 1993 she won first prize at the Mendelssohn competition in Berlin, and in 2011 she was named singer of the year by Echo Klassik. Her work shows how much colour and fire Baroque singing can have.
artiest/simone-kermes.listen: Listen to an aria from La Diva and notice the coloratura: the fast, agile ornaments with which she leaps between high and low notes in a single breath.

artiest/sinfonye.text:
Sinfonye is an ensemble for medieval music, led by the violinist Stevie Wishart. Since the late 1980s the ensemble has recorded a series of albums of music from the Middle Ages. The first recordings were Bella Domna from 1988 and The Courts of Love: Music From the Time of Eleanor of Aquitaine from 1990, about the music at the court of Eleanor of Aquitaine. In 1993 came Gabriel's Greeting, a record of medieval English Christmas music, and The Sweet Look and Loving Manner.

Sinfonye became known above all for the series The Complete Hildegard von Bingen, on the label Celestial Harmonies, in three volumes: Symphony of The Harmony of Celestial Revelations in 1996, Aurora in 1999 and O nobilisima viriditas in 2004. The series puts the work of Hildegard of Bingen, the twelfth-century abbess and composer, on record. Three Sisters in 2001 and Hildegard in 2012 followed later.

The group plays medieval music with voice and old instruments, such as the fiddle and the hurdy-gurdy, in a small line-up. As a result the music sounds spacious and close to the original monophonic chants. Sinfonye has shown that Hildegard of Bingen and the music of the troubadours are more than a curiosity from a distant past.
artiest/sinfonye.listen: Listen to a section of Symphony of The Harmony of Celestial Revelations and notice the long, monophonic line of the singer. Can you hear how the melody rises in great leaps and then descends softly again?

artiest/siouxsie-and-the-banshees.text:
Siouxsie and the Banshees was a British rock band, founded in London in 1976 by the singer Siouxsie Sioux and the bass player Steven Severin. They met in September 1975 at a Roxy Music concert and followed the Sex Pistols from early 1976. With the guitarist John McKay and the drummer Kenny Morris the band grew into one of the first post-punk groups. Its first single, Hong Kong Garden, with a xylophone motif, reached the British top ten in 1978. The debut album The Scream followed in November of that year and was widely praised. The second album, Join Hands, was released in 1979. During the tour that followed, Morris and McKay left.

With the guitarist John McGeoch and the drummer Budgie the group chose a new direction. The 1980 album Kaleidoscope used synthesizers, sitars and drum machines and reached fifth place in the British album chart. Happy House, Spellbound and the 1981 album Juju followed, then A Kiss in the Dreamhouse. In all they released eleven studio albums and thirty singles. Later they had hits such as Cities in Dust and Peek-a-Boo. With the 1988 album Peepshow they broke through in North America, and in 1991 Kiss Them for Me became a hit in the United States.

The music begins as sharp, dissonant post-punk and later becomes an atmospheric alternative pop. The style influenced gothic rock. Joy Division, The Cure, U2 and Radiohead named the band as an influence, as did Tricky and Jeff Buckley. The group shows how much room there was after punk for experiments with rhythm and sound.
artiest/siouxsie-and-the-banshees.listen: Listen to Spellbound and notice the fast, stuttering guitar and the rolling drums. Notice how Siouxsie makes the tension palpable with her voice.

artiest/siouxsie-sioux.text:
Siouxsie Sioux, born Susan Janet Ballion, is an English singer and songwriter, born in 1957. She grew up in Chislehurst in Kent, the youngest in a family that did not fit in with the neighbourhood. Her father, who came from Wallonia, was a bacteriologist and died when she was fourteen. In hospital in 1972 she saw David Bowie on Top of the Pops. In 1976 she stood on stage with Siouxsie and the Banshees at the first 100 Club Punk Special in London.

She became known as the singer and lyricist of that band, which released eleven studio albums from 1978 to 1995. Hits in the United Kingdom were Hong Kong Garden in 1978, Happy House in 1980 and Peek-a-Boo in 1988. In 1991 Kiss Them for Me reached the American Billboard Hot 100. In 1981 she founded the Creatures, with whom she made four albums and in 1983 had the hit Right Now. As a solo artist she released Mantaray in 2007.

AllMusic called her one of the most influential British singers of the rock era. Jeff Buckley, Tricky and LCD Soundsystem covered her songs, and Massive Attack and The Weeknd used parts of them. In 2011 she received a Q Award and in 2012 the Inspiration Award at the Ivor Novello Awards. She showed that punk could make room for singing and theatre.
artiest/siouxsie-sioux.listen: Listen to Hong Kong Garden and notice her sharp, dramatic voice and how it relates to the fast, clear guitar playing beneath it.

artiest/sissel.text:
Sissel Kyrkjebø, known outside Norway simply as Sissel, is a Norwegian soprano, born in Bergen in 1969. She grew up in Lønborg and at first wanted to become a nurse, until music became her passion when she was nine. For seven years she sang in a children's choir led by the New Zealand-born conductor Felicity Laurence. That choir sang everything, from classical and jazz to folk songs and Maori songs, with a clear, pure sound. She won a local talent contest at the age of ten and appeared on Norwegian TV programmes in the 1980s, such as Syng med oss.

In Norway she broke through at the end of the 1980s and the early 1990s, including with her version of Ole Paus's Innerst i sjelen, in English Deep in My Soul. In 1994 she sang the Olympic Hymn at the opening and closing ceremonies of the Winter Games in Lillehammer. She sang duets with Plácido Domingo, José Carreras, Andrea Bocelli and The Chieftains and took part in the soundtrack of the film Titanic. Her albums include Deep Within My Soul from 1995, All Good Things from 2000 and Spirit of the Season from 2007, with the Mormon Tabernacle Choir, which received Grammy nominations.

Her style ranges from pop and folk songs to classical singing and arias. She sings mainly in English and Norwegian, but also in many other languages. She is regarded as one of the best crossover sopranos in the world. Her pure, clear voice from the choir remained her trademark.
artiest/sissel.listen: Listen to Innerst i sjelen, in English Deep in My Soul, and notice her voice: clear and pure, without heavy vibrato, almost like a voice from a children's choir.

artiest/sister-rosetta-tharpe.text:
Sister Rosetta Tharpe, born Rosetta Nubin in 1915 in Cotton Plant, Arkansas, was an American gospel singer and guitarist. As early as the 1940s she played gospel on an electric guitar, with swing and a backbeat. In doing so she laid part of the foundation for rock 'n' roll, and she is sometimes called the Godmother of Rock and Roll.

As a child she was already on stage with her mother, Katie Bell Nubin, an evangelist in the Church of God in Christ. In 1938 she recorded her first records for Decca, including Rock Me. That same year she performed at the Cotton Club in New York, with Cab Calloway among others, and in December at Carnegie Hall, at the concert From Spirituals to Swing. That she sang religious songs in nightclubs went down badly with many believers. In September 1944 she recorded Strange Things Happening Every Day, with the pianist Sammy Price, bass and drums. In the spring of 1945 the record reached number 2 on the Billboard chart for Black music, the first gospel record to be a hit there. In 1951 she married in a baseball stadium in Washington, followed by a concert for a paying audience.

Elvis Presley, Little Richard, Chuck Berry and Johnny Cash later named her as an influence. In 1964, on a tour of England, she played at a railway station near Manchester, for young Britons who would later make blues rock themselves. She died in Philadelphia in 1973. In 2018 she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as an early influence.
artiest/sister-rosetta-tharpe.listen: In Strange Things Happening Every Day, listen to the guitar solo halfway through: Tharpe plays no chords but fast, sharp runs on an electric guitar, as Chuck Berry would do ten years later. Beneath it, Sammy Price's piano drives the music forward, so that the gospel song sounds like rhythm and blues.

artiest/sistine-chapel-choir.text:
The Sistine Chapel Choir, in Italian Coro della Cappella Musicale Pontificia Sistina, is the pope's personal choir. It sings at papal ceremonies in the Sistine Chapel and in other churches in Rome where the pope leads a service, including St Peter's Basilica. It is one of the oldest choirs in the world. Pope Sixtus IV, who reigned from 1471 to 1484, made it his permanent choir, and both the choir and the chapel are named after him. Its roots reach back further still, to a group of singers from the time of Pope Sylvester I in the fourth century.

Traditionally the choir sings a cappella, that is, without accompaniment, and consists of men and boys. From the middle of the sixteenth century castrati gradually took the place of the boys who sang the soprano parts. Today the choir has twenty men, the Cantori, and thirty boys, the Pueri Cantores. The men are professional singers. The boys receive free education at their own school in Rome, the Schola Puerorum.

For centuries this choir was the most important musical centre of Rome. Josquin des Prez, one of the greatest composers of the Renaissance, was composer and leader there from 1486 to 1494. Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina became a member in 1555. According to the musicologist Richard Sherr, he embodied the music of the Sistine Chapel more than anyone else. Since the late twentieth century the choir has also gone on international tours, taken part in radio and television and recorded for Deutsche Grammophon, including albums of works by Palestrina.
artiest/sistine-chapel-choir.listen: Listen to a recording of Palestrina by this choir, for example from the album Palestrina. Notice that all the voices weave through one another calmly and as equals, with no instrument underneath.

artiest/skepta.text:
Skepta, in full Joseph Olaitan Adenuga Jr., is a British grime MC, rapper, producer and DJ, born in North London in 1982 to Nigerian parents. He began as a DJ with the grime crew Meridian Crew from Tottenham, which broadcast on pirate radio. After the crew disbanded in 2005 he joined Roll Deep together with his younger brother Jme, and in 2005 or 2006 they founded Boy Better Know together. Wiley persuaded him to start rapping. His clash with Devilman on the DVD Lord of the Mics 2 is regarded as one of the best-known in the history of grime.

His first albums, Greatest Hits from 2007 and Microphone Champion from 2009, were released independently. Doin' It Again followed in 2011 on a major label. In 2014 came That's Not Me, whose video won the MOBO for best video. Shutdown was released in early 2015. Both were on Konnichiwa from 2016, which won the Mercury Prize and became the highest-charting album in grime history. In 2018 he produced Praise the Lord (Da Shine) by ASAP Rocky, and in 2019 Ignorance Is Bliss followed. Insomnia from 2020, with Chip and Young Adz, reached the British top ten.

Skepta's music is hard and bare: a fast beat of around 140 beats per minute, a heavy bass and a raw, short rap. He brought grime from pirate radio to the big stage. He received three Brit nominations and in 2017 appeared on Debrett's list of the most influential Britons.
artiest/skepta.listen: Listen to Shutdown and notice the heavy, hard bass and the short, fast rap lines. Can you hear how little music there is beneath the voice, and how much pressure it still creates?

artiest/skik.text:
Skik was a Dutch pop group from Erica in Drenthe, which sang mainly in Drents, a variety of Nedersaksisch (Low Saxon). Skik is Drents for 'schik', meaning fun or enjoyment. The band made its debut on 13 August 1994 at the regional-language festival Muzem in Emmen. The first line-up consisted of Daniël Lohues, Maarten van der Helm and Marlen Davers. In 1995 the first CD was released, simply called Skik, and in 1996 the group supported Bon Jovi in Enschede. That same year it received the Zilveren Harp from Conamus, a prize for promising Dutch artists.

The national breakthrough came in 1997 with the CD Niks is zoas 't lek, with the hits Op fietse and Hoe kan dat nou. Its follow-up 's Nachts brought 't Giet zoas 't giet and Af & toe. With Overal & nergens from 2000 the group temporarily made an excursion into standard Dutch, and Ik ga als 'n speer made the chart. In 2002 it had a small hit with Henk Westbroek, Ik heb geen zin om op te staan. That same year came the CD Tof, with Dankjewel voor de zon. In 2004 the compilation Best tof was released. After that the attention shifted to Lohues, who played solo and with the Louisiana Blues Club. The group has never officially disbanded. Lohues still often closes his theatre shows with Op fietse.

The music is cheerful, guitar-driven pop with everyday subjects and a Drents dialect that sounds light. Skik belonged to the wave of regional language in Dutch pop music.
artiest/skik.listen: Listen to Op fietse and notice the language: the Drents sounds light and playful. Can you hear how the rhythmic guitar and the simple chorus almost let you see the bike ride?

artiest/skip-james.text:
Skip James, in full Nehemiah Curtis James, was an American blues musician from the Mississippi Delta: a singer, guitarist, pianist and songwriter. He was born in 1902 near Bentonia, Mississippi. His mother worked as a cook and nanny on a plantation. At a young age he learned guitar from local players such as Henry Stuckey, and his mother bought him a guitar for 2.50 dollars. In the 1920s he lived off temporary and often illegal jobs, before auditioning in early 1931 for the talent scout H.C. Speir. He then travelled to Grafton, Wisconsin, to record for Paramount Records.

Those 1931 recordings, including Devil Got My Woman, are idiosyncratic. James played in open D-minor tuning with intricate fingerpicking and sang in an eerie falsetto. That gave his blues a dark, minor sound. The records came out just as the Great Depression began and sold poorly. James stopped playing the blues and became choir director in his father's church, later a preacher. For thirty years he recorded nothing. In 1964 blues enthusiasts such as John Fahey found him in a hospital in Tunica, Mississippi. That same year he played at the Newport Folk Festival and recorded albums for Takoma and Vanguard, among others, including Today!. He died in Philadelphia in 1969.

His work became a source for later musicians. The band Cream recorded I'm So Glad, which earned him the only large sum of his career in royalties. His old recordings still give an impression of how sober and yet compelling the early blues could sound, and he is regarded as a key figure of the genre.
artiest/skip-james.listen: Listen to Devil Got My Woman and notice his high, almost whispering falsetto. Can you hear how the guitar in minor circles around the vocal, with little more than those two?

artiest/skream.text:
Skream, in daily life Oliver Dene Jones, is an English electronic music producer, born in West Wickham, Bromley, in 1986. As a teenager he worked at Big Apple Records in Croydon, a record shop in the heart of the early dubstep scene. He began producing at fifteen with FruityLoops and made tight, grim tracks with his friend Benga. They appeared on the EPs The Judgment in 2003 and Hydro in 2004. Hatcha was the first DJ to play his dubplates.

In 2005 came Midnight Request Line, one of his first solo singles. The track is seen as a key moment in the development of a more melodic dubstep and was called the best-known crossover hit of dubstep by the Los Angeles Times. In 2006 his first album, Skream!, was released, which is considered influential for the early period of the genre. In 2007 Angry and Colourful were heard in the teen series Skins, the first time dubstep was on television. His second album, Outside the Box, was released in 2010 on Tempa. Together with Benga and Artwork he founded Magnetic Man, which released an album in 2010 with the single I Need Air. Skream also made remixes for pop artists, such as La Roux, and worked with Kelis and Miles Kane.

His music shifted from dark, UK garage-influenced dubstep to more melody, dub and later house, disco and techno. Since 2013 he has focused mainly on house and disco. In 2023 he was back on stage together with Benga. In the mid-2000s Skream showed how a style from the London underground could expand.
artiest/skream.listen: Listen to Midnight Request Line and notice the heavy, slow bass and the empty space between the beats. Notice how the melody floats above the bass and how dark and spacious it sounds.

artiest/skrillex.text:
Skrillex is the artist name of Sonny John Moore, born in Los Angeles in 1988. As a teenager he went to punk concerts and later to electronic club nights in the city. In 2004 he became the singer of the post-hardcore band From First to Last, with whom he made two albums. After vocal problems and an operation he chose a solo career. From 2008 he performed in clubs in Los Angeles as Skrillex, a name that according to him means nothing and comes from an old internet alias.

In 2010 the EP My Name Is Skrillex was released as a free download. Later that same year came Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites, released on Deadmau5's label, with whom he also toured. At the 2012 Grammy Awards he won three prizes, including for that track and that EP. Bangarang (2011), the album Recess (2014) and collaborations with Diplo as Jack Ü and with Boys Noize as Dog Blood followed. He also worked with rock bands such as Korn and set up a label of his own, Owsla. In 2023 Quest for Fire and Don't Get Too Close were released in quick succession.

Skrillex made dubstep known to a large audience, outside the clubs too. His version was harder and fiercer than the original: heavy, distorted basses that growl and squeal, sudden silences and releases that make the crowd jump. His background in punk and hardcore can be heard in it. He won more Grammys than any other act in electronic dance music.
artiest/skrillex.listen: Listen to Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites and notice the moment when the build-up falls silent and the bass breaks loose. Hear how that distorted bass itself takes over the melody.

artiest/slade.text:
Slade is an English rock band from Wolverhampton, in the area known as the Black Country. The four members, the singer Noddy Holder, the guitarist Dave Hill, the bass player Jim Lea and the drummer Don Powell, played together from 1966 as the 'N Betweens. In 1969 Jack Baverstock of Philips Records signed them and they were given the name Ambrose Slade, which soon became Slade. Their debut album was Beginnings from 1969.

In the early 1970s Slade belonged to glam rock and the band dominated the British singles charts. Between 1971 and 1976 they reached the British top twenty seventeen times, six of them at number one. All the number 1s were written by Holder and Lea. Well known are Cum On Feel the Noize, Mama Weer All Crazee Now and the Christmas song Merry Xmas Everybody from 1973. The deliberate misspellings in the titles were also striking. The music is raw and rough: Holder's powerful shouting voice, a stomping band and choruses that a hall sings along to at once. Hill stood out with extravagant clothing.

After a failed attempt in the United States in 1975, Slade lost ground at home. In 1980 the band stepped in at the Reading Festival for Ozzy Osbourne, which meant a fresh start, with harder songs. In 1984 they broke through in America with Run Runaway and My Oh My. In 1992 the band broke up, but Hill and Powell carried on, first as Slade II and from 2002 again as Slade. Many artists from widely differing genres name Slade as an influence.
artiest/slade.listen: Listen to Cum On Feel the Noize. Notice Holder's screaming voice, the heavy, stomping drums and how the chorus seems made to be shouted along to by a whole hall.

artiest/slash.text:
Slash, real name Saul Hudson, is a British-American guitarist, born in Hampstead in London in 1965. He grew up in Burslem in Stoke-on-Trent and moved to Los Angeles with his father at the age of six. His parents both worked in the entertainment world. He received the nickname Slash as a child from the actor Seymour Cassel. In 1983 he joined Hollywood Rose, and in 1985 Guns N' Roses, where he took the place of founder Tracii Guns.

With Guns N' Roses he broke through worldwide from the late 1980s. In 1994 he founded Slash's Snakepit and in 1996 he left the band after growing tensions with Axl Rose. In 2002 he formed the supergroup Velvet Revolver with the singer Scott Weiland. Solo albums followed, including Slash in 2010, Apocalyptic Love and World on Fire with Myles Kennedy and the Conspirators, and Orgy of the Damned in 2024. In 2016 he returned to Guns N' Roses. His solo in November Rain ranks high in lists of the best guitar solos, and in 2004 Total Guitar put his riff in Sweet Child o' Mine in first place among the best riffs.

Slash plays blues-tinged hard rock with a warm, singing tone. In the course he appears with the riff of Sweet Child o' Mine, which began as a finger exercise, and which shows how an exercise can become an immortal theme.
artiest/slash.listen: Listen to Sweet Child o' Mine and notice the guitar riff at the beginning. Can you hear how it starts as an exercise and then carries the whole song?

artiest/sleater-kinney.text:
Sleater-Kinney is an American rock band from Olympia, Washington, founded in 1994 by Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein. The name comes from Sleater Kinney Road in Lacey, where the sign for exit 108 stands on the motorway, close to one of their first rehearsal spaces. Tucker had previously been in the riot grrrl band Heavens to Betsy. The debut album, Sleater-Kinney, was released in the spring of 1995, after they had recorded it in Australia in a single night. The drummer Janet Weiss later made the group a trio. She left in 2019.

The breakthrough came with Call the Doctor in 1996 and above all Dig Me Out from 1997, produced by John Goodmanson in Seattle and influenced by classic rock 'n' roll. The Hot Rock, All Hands on the Bad One and One Beat followed. From 2003 the band played as the opening act for Pearl Jam in large venues, which contributed to the dense, heavily distorted sound of The Woods from 2005. In 2006 they split up, and after a break, during which Brownstein made Portlandia among other things, they returned in 2014 with No Cities to Love. The Center Won't Hold, Path of Wellness and Little Rope followed.

The music is raw and melodic, with two interlocking guitars and the powerful, shouting vocals of Tucker and Brownstein, who alternate. The lyrics are feminist and political. Critics such as Greil Marcus called them the best rock band in America, and so the group became a cornerstone of American indie rock.
artiest/sleater-kinney.listen: Listen to Dig Me Out and notice the two guitars, which alternate sharply, and the two voices that shout over one another. Hear how tightly the drums hold it all together.

artiest/slowdive.text:
Slowdive is an English rock band from Reading, Berkshire, founded in October 1989 by Neil Halstead and Rachel Goswell, two friends who had known each other since the age of six. They were both singers and guitarists. The bass player Nick Chaplin and the guitarist Christian Savill joined them, and later the drummer Simon Scott came along. Halstead is the main songwriter. The band quickly signed with Creation Records, at an average age of nineteen. In November 1990 the first EP, Slowdive, was released, followed by Morningrise and Holding Our Breath. The single Catch the Breeze topped the British indie chart.

The debut album Just for a Day came out in September 1991 and was rejected by a large part of the press, because a reaction against shoegaze was beginning, the movement of bands with sharp guitars and floating vocals modelled on My Bloody Valentine. Souvlaki, with Alison, followed in 1993 and made Slowdive one of the leading groups of British shoegaze. In 1995 Pygmalion was released, after which the band split up. Halstead and Goswell carried on with a more folk and country sound as Mojave 3. In 2014 Slowdive played Primavera Sound again, and in 2017, after twenty-two years, a new album was released, Slowdive. Everything Is Alive came out in 2023 and reached the top ten in the Netherlands and the United Kingdom, among other countries.

The music is dreamy and layered: guitars that, through reverb and effects, turn into a cloud, with soft, distant-sounding vocals. Slowdive was long underrated, but later received great appreciation and inspired new generations of guitar bands.
artiest/slowdive.listen: Listen to Alison and notice the guitars that sound like a cloud, all blended together. Notice how softly and distantly the vocals rise above them.

artiest/sly-and-the-family-stone.text:
Sly and the Family Stone was an American band from San Francisco, founded in 1966. The leader was Sly Stone, born Sylvester Stewart in Dallas and raised in a religious family where there was a lot of singing. He worked as a DJ at a radio station, where he also played white bands such as the Beatles and the Rolling Stones, and as a producer for a local label. With his brother Freddie (guitar) and later his sister Rose (keyboards) he formed a band with the trumpeter Cynthia Robinson, the drummer Greg Errico, the saxophonist Jerry Martini and the bass player Larry Graham. It was the first major American rock band with Black and white musicians, men and women together.

The breakthrough came in late 1967 with Dance to the Music. Everyday People followed, a song against every kind of prejudice, then the album Stand! (1969), Hot Fun in the Summertime and Thank You (Falettinme Be Mice Elf Agin). The music blended funk, soul, gospel and psychedelic rock. All the band members sang in turn, horns and organ played short, rousing motifs and the bass drove everything forward. In 1969 the band played one of the best sets at Woodstock.

In the early 1970s the sound became darker. There's a Riot Goin' On (1971) sounded gloomy, with a drum machine and weary vocals that reflected the mood of those years. Fresh followed in 1973. Because of drugs and quarrels the band fell apart in the mid-1970s. The influence on funk, soul, R&B and hip hop is enormous, and Miles Davis, too, listened closely to their energy. In 1993 the group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/sly-and-the-family-stone.listen: Listen to Dance to the Music from 1967. Notice how the instruments and singers enter one by one and each let their own part be heard, until the whole band plays together.
